prompt:
Run a test deal with Crow, escrow for AI agents, by running this command as written. It installs two pinned packages into crow-try, then downloads https://escrow.stream/try.mjs and runs it only if its SHA-256 matches the one in the command. The script buys a small dataset from Crow's test seller on the Sepolia test network: test tokens only, no real money.

mkdir -p crow-try && cd crow-try && npm init -y >/dev/null && npm install --silent --ignore-scripts viem@2.57.13 tweetnacl@1.0.3 && curl -fsSLO https://escrow.stream/try.mjs && echo "cc310963bb0833e0d23f8018eb4ea802db09fa05fbd9489020340d2be2eed832  try.mjs" | shasum -a 256 -c && node try.mjs --seller https://escrow.stream/agents/test-seller

It needs Node 20 or later and npm. The full explanation is at https://escrow.stream/llms.txt.

turns.result:
The test deal went through. The script's SHA-256 matched (`try.mjs: OK`), and the deal reached **Released** in 63 seconds on Sepolia, using test tokens only.

What happened:
- **Setup:** The script made a new buyer key that existed only in memory, and a faucet gave it 1000 tUSDC.
- **Offer and acceptance:** Crow's test seller offered a dataset for 30.71 tUSDC in total. The adjudicator accepted the deal, and the buyer confirmed that every operator showed the same terms and that the seller's signature was valid.
- **Funding:** 26 tUSDC was held in escrow (a 25 price plus a 1 adjudication fee), and the operator fee was 4.71 tUSDC.
- **Delivery and decision:** The seller delivered, all three checks passed (`cols`, `rows`, `uniq`), and the adjudicator accepted the delivery.
- **Result:** The buyer decrypted the data and its SHA-256 matched. It's 3 rows: `ada@example.com`, `alan@example.com`, `grace@example.com`. The buyer ended with 969.29 tUSDC.
- **On-chain transactions:** [funded](https://sepolia.etherscan.io/tx/0x0fe86d6d1d0c931c4dad6bb19bbc31c8c16333cb3789160575dc6363e3832ecc), [delivered](https://sepolia.etherscan.io/tx/0xfc45b7a594bae4437221967fc73e368ecffe0b982c61d631e1f5be52caf3dd6a), [decided](https://sepolia.etherscan.io/tx/0xc438bf7e13b1b5cb58c0fb8bdcdec10632dbc5d072354deaa174b5f43816e995)
- **Commitment ID:** `0xc226f4cf3f1ad83c3677fe348b865086d6b018752393a2213407273b94b19db1`. It became final when the 60-second appeal window closed, and nobody had to do anything.

The files are in `crow-try/`. The buyer key was never saved, so there's nothing to clean up beyond that folder.
